claim: PerformLine is an omni-channel marketing-compliance platform operating in two phases: automated PRE-publication review ('Reduce manual review time by 90%... with automated pre-publication review', 'near-instant feedback on materials... corrected before it goes live') and POST-publication monitoring ('Continuously discover where your offers and brand appear', including 'AI responses, web, social, email, and partner channels'); channels: web, social, email, calls, SMS/chat messages, documents (PPT, Word, PDF, MP4, Google Docs, JPG).
notes: Dual pre/post model is the category-defining shape. Review object is always a marketing ASSET or conversation, never a transaction/action.

claim: PerformLine claims 'Trusted by 6 of the top 10 U.S. banks'; supported verticals on site: Banks, Credit Cards, Fintech, Mortgage; named customer quote from Acima VP of Compliance.
notes: Confirms the synthesis session's homepage verification; enterprise penetration of the exact buyer set Candidates 1/2 target (bank/fintech compliance).

claim: Rulebooks are vendor-curated in-house: 'Refined with experience and a track record of success across client compliance programs since 2007', 'Built on years of experience with regulators and clients', and 'crafted from regulatory bulletins, acts, documents, settlements, and industry standards from governing bodies including the CFPB, FTC, FCC, SEC, ED, OCC, FINRA and more'.
notes: Provenance is claimed at the corpus level (sources: bulletins/acts/settlements) but NO per-rule citation graph, versioning, or update-cadence documentation is exposed publicly.

claim: Rulebook regulatory coverage is federal-act based: Dodd-Frank, UDAAP, CARD Act, TCPA, Higher Education Act, TILA, RESPA, FTC Act, MAP Rule/Reg N, ERISA, GLBA, CARES Act, Patriot Act, FDCPA, SAFE Act; industries listed: Banking, BNPL, Credit Card, Mortgage, FinTech, Alternative Lending, Gig-Economy, Education, Technology, Healthcare. No state-level jurisdiction packs and no gambling/gaming industry listed.
notes: The jurisdiction axis is regulator/act-level, not US-state-level. Absence of state packs and of gambling vertical is absence-on-the-enumerating-page (the page lists its coverage), so stronger than silence.

claim: Customers can add custom rules: 'Add your own rules to meet your enterprise compliance needs — and manage them directly in your system of record, with PerformLine staying in sync'.
notes: Hybrid model: vendor-curated base + customer-authored extensions.

claim: Pre-publication review scores assets 0-100 mapping to 'Pass, Warning, or Fail state, with client-configurable thresholds'; each finding includes 'the violation type, the affected snippet, the regulatory basis, and a severity level, along with a plain-language explanation' plus 'a suggested compliant rewrite'; built-in 'UDAAP, CAN-SPAM, and Schumer Box / TILA rule packs'.
notes: Tri-state verdict semantics exist here — but on CONTENT, advisory, human-consumed; not an allow/deny/review decision binding an action at runtime.

claim: The pre-publication gate is advisory (suggested rewrites; no documented hard publication block) and embeds into content workflows: 'Deploy prepublication reviews directly in your workflow, or tools like Figma, or upload directly to PerformLine'; integrations with Workfront, monday.com, Jira, Aprimo, Smartsheet, Asana, 'Zapier app or any API-driven tool'.
notes: 'Advisory' is inference from the absence of any blocking claim on the product page; enforcement of the gate is organizational (workflow), not technical.

claim: Workflow/audit story: remediation notices sent from the platform to 'non-compliant partners, agents, or reps' with responses 'recorded within the workflow for one seamless trackable history'; 'Archive for the length you require, a complete history of discovery through remediation for any audit situation'; alert states from 'not reviewed through resolved'.
notes: Audit story = asset-review and remediation history with configurable retention. No policy-version binding, no attestation semantics, no as-of replay claimed.

claim: Integrations page: 'Out-of-the-box connectors, webhooks, and APIs that bring discovery, review, and evidence into your existing stack'; task-system pushback ('Create issues in your task system with context from the flagged asset and the rule that triggered it'); call/message systems supported: Intercom, RingCentral, Five9, NICE, Twilio, Genesys, RingClone, LiveVox, Verint. No public developer portal, no programmatic verdict/decision endpoint documented.
notes: APIs exist for asset submission/finding export — workflow plumbing, not a runtime authorization API. Absence of decision API is absence-of-documentation, corroborated by product model.

claim: Company: founded 2007 by Alex Baydin, HQ Morristown NJ; backed by First Round Capital (2007), strategic investment from M33 Growth (May 2021), and 'additional funding received January 2026 to accelerate AI product expansion plans'; positions as 'The Leader in Automated Marketing Compliance'.
notes: 19-year-old category incumbent with fresh capital earmarked for AI expansion — fast-follow capacity into adjacent review surfaces.

claim: PerformLine's marketing-compliance learning hub covers UDAAP, Dodd-Frank, FTC Act, TILA, CARD Act, TCPA, fintech-bank partnerships, BaaS, BNPL, call centers, complaints — and contains NO coverage of sweepstakes, contests, giveaways, promotions law, prize law, state-level promotional rules, or gambling/gaming marketing.
notes: Directly answers red-team question 7's sub-question: PerformLine's rulebooks/editorial footprint do NOT extend to promotions/sweepstakes conduct law. Absence verified on the enumerating hub page; MEDIUM because a paid rulebook could exist unpublicized.

claim: Regulatory bodies monitored for rulebook inputs include CFPB, FTC, OCC, SEC, FINRA, FCC, FDIC, Dept. of Labor, Dept. of Education, UK FCA, and 'State Attorneys General'.
notes: State AGs are monitored as an enforcement-signal source for content rules — not as per-state statutory rule packs.

claim: No PerformLine product or resource references sweepstakes/contest/promotions-law rulebooks anywhere findable (rulebooks page, learn hub, web search 'PerformLine sweepstakes contests promotions rulebook' returns only law-firm and promo-agency content, no PerformLine assets).
notes: Triangulated absence (two official enumerating pages + search). Inference: PerformLine reviews promotional COPY under UDAAP/FTC deception standards but does not maintain promotional-CONDUCT law content (registration/bonding, AMOE, prize thresholds).

claim: Red Marker (redmarker.ai) automates compliance review of advertising/marketing content pre-publication and during authoring: document scanning, approvals module ('Red Marker Approvals'), web reports; positions 'ensure only compliant content reaches the market'; industry rule libraries referenced include 'FINRA Marketing Compliance', 'FCA Marketing Compliance', and an 'Australian Retail Banking' risk rule library; industries: financial services, insurance, automotive, telecom, food & beverage, pharma, healthcare.
notes: The closest thing found to productized jurisdiction/regulator-scoped rule libraries for marketing content — but scoped to regulator regimes (US FINRA, UK FCA, AU banking), not US-state granularity, and to ad copy, not conduct.

claim: Rules are applied/maintained by the vendor's own teams with customer input: 'Client Success and Implementation teams apply and customize rules and requirements, training the AI model on the triggers to identify risks'; scanning flags 'misleading phrases and unsubstantiated claims', 'high-risk words & phrases', 'incorrect or missing disclaimers and disclosures', and 'unclear promotions'; scanning happens during creation (Word/Figma plug-ins) and pre-approval.
notes: 'Unclear promotions' shows promotional AD-COPY checks exist; no per-rule statutory citation/provenance documented publicly.

claim: Red Marker's public API (redmarkertech.github.io/api-docs) is an asynchronous asset-review API: resources are Assets, Reviews, Webhooks; assets (PDF, docx, etc.) are submitted, reviews performed separately, results/'Review PDF' returned later via push or pull — a content-scanning API, not a synchronous decision endpoint.
notes: Confirms architecture: document-review pipeline. Unsuitable as a runtime action-authorization API (async, asset-scoped).

claim: IntelligenceBank (marketing operations/DAM SaaS) acquired Red Marker on July 29, 2024, including technology, IP, and teams in Australia, Canada, US, UK; strategy: 'a single platform to ensure all marketing content—across print, social, email, and digital—is brand and legally approved'. Press coverage: Red Marker was founded by Matt Symons, sold to Kaplan in March 2017, sold by Kaplan to IntelligenceBank in 2024.
page_title: Red Marker acquired by IntelligenceBank (+ Startup Daily / Business News Australia coverage)
notes: The 'Red Marker (Kaplan)' framing in the assignment is outdated: Kaplan exited July 2024. New owner's strategy folds compliance review INTO marketing-ops tooling (brand + legal approval), pointing away from conduct authorization.

claim: SaifrReview reviews text, images, and video at creation time ('Run compliance scans as content is created' via add-ins) and in centralized pre-publication review; regulatory scope named: 'FINRA 2210', 'SEC 482', 'SEC Modernized Marketing Rule'; risk categories: 'promissory, misleading, exaggerated, or unwarranted' language, performance claims, testimonials, comparisons.
notes: Regulator-rule-scoped AI review for US financial-services marketing content; banking and insurance/annuities variants exist.

claim: Saifr 'was born in Fidelity Labs, the in-house software incubator at Fidelity Investments'; models 'trained on 20+ years of proprietary, industry-unique data from regulatory and compliance experts'; global team across Boston, NY, Texas, Dublin, Chennai, Bangalore.
notes: Rule source is a learned model over Fidelity's internal compliance-review corpus — provenance is institutional experience, not statute citations. Fidelity balance sheet behind it.

claim: Saifr exposes its review as an API: 'API: Build compliance risk scanning into your processes'; available in the Microsoft Azure AI model catalog; partnerships with Adobe and ServiceNow.
notes: The most API-first vendor in the category — but the API returns content-risk findings on submitted material, not action verdicts. Azure catalog distribution makes it embeddable in third-party workflows.

claim: Saifr performance claims: 'Instantly detect up to 90% of what a human would', 'Bring more compliant content to market up to 10x faster', 'in seconds'; named customer: Nasdaq (regulatory compliance AVP testimonial).
notes: Marketing claims, unaudited; establishes that the category sells 'detect most of what a human reviewer would' as the value metric — assistive, not authoritative.

claim: Luthor (luthor.ai) scans 'every asset before publication, from internal drafts to customer content across every channel' (text, images, video, audio, SMS, social, URLs) against built-in regulatory frameworks (FINRA, FTC, FCA, UDAAP, GDPR; FINRA 2210 named) plus customer policies and approved knowledge bases; pre-publication only; 'Clear evidence for every decision'.
page_title: Luthor — Marketing Compliance Platform for Regulated Industries
notes: AI-native entrant; homepage stat counters appeared as placeholder/animated values ('$0+ AUM Protected', '340% Fines Avoided YoY') — treat all quantified traction claims as LOW confidence.

claim: Luthor is a Y Combinator company founded 2024 (San Francisco); YC positions it as 'AI compliance infrastructure for regulated marketing' and 'real-time governance for enterprise communications'; reported ~$500K raised with investors including Drive Capital, Tribe Capital, TQ Ventures, YC; platform scans marketing against SEC, FINRA, FinCEN rules with 'expert human oversight from former SEC attorneys'; clients described as RIAs/broker-dealers with >$5.7B combined AUM.
page_title: Luthor — Y Combinator profile (+ Tracxn/Crunchbase funding data)
notes: Seed-stage, RIA-scale traction ($5.7B AUM across clients is small-firm territory). 'Compliance infrastructure' framing + attorney-in-the-loop model is the C1-adjacent ambition at embryo scale.

claim: Red Oak (redoak.com) claims '1800+ Firms Globally' and 'Partner to Over Half of the Top 20 Asset Managers'; 84 NPS; buyers: broker-dealers, RIAs, banks, insurance.
notes: The volume incumbent of pre-publication advertising review workflow in US financial services — discovered during this supplement; not in the original 15-company set or the assignment's named list.

claim: Red Oak products: 'advertising review software that increases the accuracy and effectiveness of compliance reviews', AI Review leveraging 'Large Language Models (LLMs) and sophisticated prompt engineering', Disclosure Management, Registration Management, Internet Supervision, Social Media Compliance, Website Monitoring; 'Seamless FINRA integration'; keeps 'books and records compliant'.
notes: Workflow-first DNA: submission→review→approval chains with FINRA filing and books-and-records retention — the regulated approval-workflow muscle, applied to marketing assets.

claim: Red Oak's public pages do not claim a vendor-curated statutory rulebook: review logic is firm-configured workflow plus LLM-assisted 'AI Review'; no per-rule regulatory citation library, no jurisdiction packs documented.
notes: INFERENCE from absence on the enumerating product pages: Red Oak sells the review WORKFLOW and AI assistance; the rule substance remains the customer's compliance manual. Opposite pole from PerformLine's curated-rulebook model.

claim: Sedric.ai is 'an AI-powered platform that gives teams in regulated industries real-time guardrails on all of your content': pre-publication marketing review ('Review and approve marketing content before it goes live'), post-call QA ('automatically review every interaction'), 'Real Time Agent Assist' to 'guide agents in real time', and partner-content monitoring; sectors: fintechs/neobanks, financial institutions, crypto, ARM/collections, trading.
page_title: Sedric — AI Compliance Platform for Financial Services
notes: Real-time agent-assist is the closest thing in this category to conduct-time intervention — but the object is a human conversation, not a transaction; no decision API for actions.

claim: Sedric 'ingests and structures your policies, translating them into preventive, detective, and corrective controls' and ships 'built-in regulation libraries' spanning UDAAP, Reg Z, TILA, ECOA, FTC, CFPB, SEC, FINRA, FCA, ESMA, MiFID, MiCA, FDCPA; enforcement is applied 'manually and automatically'; 'every override is logged with reasoning, and every resolution is exam-ready by design'.
page_title: Sedric — AI Compliance Platform for Financial Services
notes: Policy-to-controls translation language ('preventive, detective, corrective') is policy-ops vocabulary one step from executable policy — the most C1-flavored positioning in the category. Regulation libraries are framework-level, not US-state-level.

claim: Sedric raised an $18.5M Series A led by Foundation Capital with American Express participation; customers include eToro, WebBank, NinjaTrader, Coastal Bank, Exness, Capital.com; case metrics: 92% increase in interaction coverage, 100% communications coverage vs sample-based review.
page_title: Sedric — AI Compliance Platform for Financial Services
notes: Funding widely press-corroborated. Customer set overlaps Candidate 4's fintech/trading target list (eToro, WebBank are exactly the regulated-adjacency profile).

claim: Haast (haast.io) does both pre-publication review ('reviewing content and communications before they go live') and post-publication monitoring ('Monitor all live assets and channels for compliance issues - including partners, influencers, and anyone linked to your brand'); handles the 'full compliance lifecycle, from intake to decision to audit trail'; implementation is 'attorney-led' by in-house legal team; native integrations (Figma, Office365, Workfront, Google Docs, monday.com) plus API.
notes: Australian-origin enterprise entrant; 'attorney-led' configuration is a counsel-in-the-loop SETUP model (counsel configures rules once), not counsel-as-approver-per-change.

claim: Haast ships pre-configured compliance 'agents' per regulatory framework, including for GAMING: 'Gambling Commission LCCP, Age Verification, Responsible Gaming'; other libraries: FINRA, FTC, FCA, UDAAP, Consumer Duty (financial services), CCPA/GDPR/Consumer Rights Act (retail), Ofcom/PECR (telecom), FDA/HIPAA (pharma).
notes: First vendor found productizing GAMBLING ADVERTISING rule content (UK LCCP marketing/social responsibility codes) — jurisdiction-scoped promotional-marketing content for Candidate 4's vertical, at the ad-copy layer only. MEDIUM: framework names from homepage marketing, depth unverified.

claim: Proofpoint Patrol reviews social posts, texts, and mobile comms with 'Pre-review or post-review options'; can 'Automatically or manually remove content directly from monitored social media accounts' and 'Automatically remove problematic content that makes its way to mobile and text messaging and public platforms'; ships 'compliance policy templates, covering FCA, FINRA, SEC, IIROC and more'; 'ensures a record of it all makes it into your archive for storage and e-discovery'.
notes: The only vendor found with automated ENFORCEMENT — but enforcement = deleting published content (content remediation), not preventing an action. Sits inside Proofpoint's digital-communications-governance (archiving/supervision) suite.

claim: Smarsh's product line is Capture, Archive, Surveillance, Discovery, Supervision — communications capture/archiving/supervision; third-party competitive analysis states 'Smarsh does not review marketing before it publishes' and places it in the archiving/surveillance camp vs purpose-built pre-publication advertising-review platforms.
page_title: Advertising Compliance Software: FINRA 2210 & SEC Rules (AdClear blog)
notes: Source is a competitor's comparison blog — bias possible, but consistent with Smarsh's own product navigation (no ad-review module found). Smarsh's marketing-rule content is thought-leadership steering to supervision/archiving products. Note: Hearsay Systems went to Yext, not Smarsh (see MKTCOMP-034).

claim: Yext announced acquisition of Hearsay Systems on June 10, 2024 for $125M plus up to $95M earnout; completed August 1, 2024. Hearsay provides 'compliant engagement solutions' for financial services across social media, websites, text, and voice (Hearsay Social, Hearsay Relate), including supervision coverage for testimonials/endorsements under the SEC Marketing Rule.
page_title: Yext Completes Acquisition of Hearsay Systems (+ PLANADVISER marketing-rule coverage)
notes: Adviser-level social publishing with pre-approved content libraries and supervision — field-comms compliance, consolidated into a digital-presence vendor. No conduct/transaction relevance.

claim: Veeva Vault PromoMats is 'a regulated content management application that supports the full lifecycle of promotional content': creation, MLR (medical-legal-regulatory) review and approval, digital asset management, claims management; can 'Easily publish and withdraw content to digital channels'; 'automatically generates eCTD compliance packages for post-marketing and pre-clearance submission to the FDA'; customers include Moderna, J&J, Gilead, GSK ('450+ top and emerging biopharmas' cited on page).
notes: The archetype: pharma proves a HARD pre-publication gate with counsel/regulatory reviewers in the loop, claim-to-reference provenance, versioned audit trails, regulator submission packaging — as a mandatory, industry-standard product. All of it scoped to promotional MATERIALS, never to transactions.

claim: AdComplyRx is a 'media optimization and compliance monitoring solution' for pharma paid-search (SEM) and social ads — 'Pharma SEM Regulatory & Brand Safety'; monitors live ads against FDA standards (cites FDA Warning Letter risk; '2020 Brand Safety Report' finding 'Over 60 major Rx brands are inadvertently running non-compliant ads on Google and Bing'); offers a Chrome extension for ad-hoc checks; LinkedIn lists 2-10 employees, NYC.
page_title: MyAdComplyRx — Pharma SEM Regulatory & Brand Safety (+ LinkedIn company page)
notes: Vertical micro-tool: post-publication channel monitoring for one ad format; positions itself as relieving 'long CMLR/PRC/PRT/PromoMats reviews' — i.e., it orbits Veeva-style MLR gates rather than replacing them. adcomplyrx.com returned 503 twice; data from mirror site + search.

claim: '4L Labs' / 'CommsCompliance' could not be identified as a real, material marketing-compliance vendor: web search returns no company by either name in this category (nearest hits: 4Comply, a marketing PRIVACY/consent tool by 4Thought Marketing, and generic category listicles).
page_title: Web search: '4L Labs' OR 'CommsCompliance' marketing compliance software
notes: Assignment-named vendor appears to be a phantom/garbled reference. Replaced in this report by the material peers actually found: Red Oak, Sedric, Haast (+ AdClear noted in landscape).

claim: Riskified and Signifyd are ecommerce fraud-prevention / chargeback-guarantee / policy-abuse vendors; no marketing-content compliance review product exists in their public positioning. Riskified.com returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch; assessment rests on their established positioning and their prior treatment in this project's landscape.
notes: INFERENCE, labeled as such: transaction-fraud decisioning vendors are out of category for marketing-compliance review; their relevance to the candidates (runtime decisioning precedent) was already covered by the main study's fraud-stack analysis. Excluded per assignment guidance ('don't force it').
